_provenance: Fictional demo data. Cost and effort figures are fixture-authored, rough planning estimates for the Sift 'Home Energy Guardian' hackathon scenario and do not describe any real service pricing.

options.label: Monitor for one more billing cycle
options.description: Take no action and observe whether the next bill remains elevated. Lowest-cost, lowest-effort option, but leaves the suspected root cause (possible thermostat malfunction) unaddressed and unresolved evidence gaps open, including whether a household or appliance event explains the spike.

options.label: Switch to a different rate plan
options.description: Evaluate and switch to an alternate tariff (for example, a time-of-use plan) that may reduce cost for this household's usage pattern. Addresses only the rate-change portion of the anomaly (18.62 USD of the 92.12 USD gap versus the prior tariff at baseline usage); does not reduce the underlying elevated usage.
options.estimatedTimeToInsight: immediate for the plan comparison; savings realized starting the next cycle

options.label: Request a home energy audit
options.description: Schedule a broad professional walkthrough assessment of insulation, air sealing, and major appliances. Thorough but slower and more expensive than a targeted HVAC/thermostat visit, and not specifically aimed at the supported thermostat-malfunction hypothesis.
options.estimatedTimeToInsight: 1-2 weeks to schedule, half-day on-site visit
options.consequentialActionNote: Scheduling the audit itself is a real-world appointment; this fixture only supports Sift proposing the option, not booking it.

options.label: Request an HVAC / thermostat inspection
options.description: Schedule a targeted technician visit to diagnose and, if confirmed, repair the suspected thermostat sensor-drift fault identified in household-events.json. Directly targets the supported hypothesis for the unexplained 280 kWh of usage in the current cycle.
options.consequentialActionNote: Creating this as a proposal requires human confirmation before it exists as a case artifact. The demo does not schedule an actual appointment; it only creates and approves the proposal record.
